subject: FintechCo RTBF / data retention follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintechco.com>, Mark Lee <mark.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo RTBF / data retention follow-up & next steps

Thanks again for the call today - great to meet the FintechCo team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of ask
- FintechCo needs an RTBF workflow for customer deletion requests (end-user level) with clear purge timelines and an auditable trail.
- Must surface what we persist in logs, retention windows for backups, and options for immediate irrecoverability if required by legal.
- Data residency requirement: primary production in us-east-1; must confirm that backups and logs remain in the same region or provide controls to restrict cross-region copies.

Redwood proposed approach (high level)
- Live data purge: remove user data from primary store within 48 hours of a validated RTBF request.
- Indexes and caches: invalidate and scrub within 7 days (rolling job).
- Backups: standard snapshot retention is 90 days. For customers requiring faster irrecoverability, we offer a key-shredding option that renders backups unreadable earlier - need legal sign-off.
- Audit logs: retain per account audit trails for 1 year by default; can export a compliance report on-demand.

Attachments: RTBF_process_diagram.pdf (flow + proposed MOP)

Next steps
1) Can you confirm FintechCo's required purge SLA for live data and for backups? (Sarah / Legal)
2) If the 30-day backup window is non-negotiable, we'll flag potential technical/legal implications and prepare an alternative (key shred + attestation).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week (I'll propose times) with Mateo and Rishi to go over implementation details and timelines.

I'll also draft a short mutual action plan and share it once we have confirmation on the backup requirement.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintechco.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo RTBF / data retention follow-up & next steps

Thanks Camila - helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- FintechCo policy (driven by Legal) requires a maximum of 30 days for customer-accessible data to be purged from live systems. Backups are a separate constraint: our security policy allows up to 90 days retention for backups, but Legal has asked whether Redwood can provide a mechanism to ensure data is irrecoverable sooner if requested.
- We also need a signed attestation that all logs referencing PII are scrubbed or redacted as part of the RTBF process.
- Data residency: we require that backups remain within the US (preferably us-east-1). Cross-region replication must be disabled for our account.

Attaching the privacy questionnaire for your legal/engineering review: privacy_questionnaire.xlsx

Can you confirm whether the live-data purge + key-shred option is feasible? If you can send a proposed mutual action plan and a short implementation timeline we can share with Legal.

- Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance, FintechCo
sarah.kim@fintechco.com

Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo RTBF / data retention follow-up & next steps

Sarah - thanks for the details and for the questionnaire. Looping in our infra and security leads to confirm feasibility. 

Quoted for context:
> FintechCo policy (driven by Legal) requires a maximum of 30 days for customer-accessible data to be purged from live systems. Backups... up to 90 days retention... can Redwood provide mechanism to ensure data is irrecoverable sooner if requested?

Mateo / Rishi / Priyom - can you weigh in on the following items so I can get back to Sarah + Legal with a concrete plan and timelines: 
1) Confirm we can guarantee live-data purge (primary DB + object store pointers) within 48 hours of validated RTBF. Any caveats?
2) Index and cache invalidation window: realistic SLA to scrub secondary indexes and search indices?
3) Backups: current snapshot retention policy and options for early irrecoverability (key destruction, crypto-shred).
4) Are there any constraints around disabling cross-region replication for a given account?

I'll draft a mutual action plan once we have answers and propose times for a technical deep-dive this week.

Thanks - Camila

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo RTBF / data retention follow-up & next steps

Camila - quick answers below (Happy to jump on the deep-dive):

1) Live-data purge: Yes - we can implement a validated RTBF flow that removes user records from the primary DB and object store references within 48 hours. Caveat: downstream analytics replicas (nearline) may have copies; we will include replica purge as part of the workflow and mark as high priority (target 7 days for full propagation).

2) Indexes/caches: We can invalidate caches immediately and schedule a rolling reindex/scrub; realistic SLA to fully remove from search/indexes is 5-7 business days depending on dataset size.

3) Backups: Standard snapshot rotation is 90 days. For customers requiring earlier irrecoverability, we have two options: 
   - Key shredding / crypto-shred: destroy the encryption keys for the affected snapshots, rendering data unreadable. This provides practical irrecoverability ahead of the retention window but requires Legal to accept a technical attestation in lieu of physical deletion.
   - Accelerated purge: maintain a separate short-retention backup policy per-account (e.g., 30 days) but this requires changes to backup policy and a provisioning lead time (~2 weeks) and could have cost implications.

We can provide an attestation template for key-shred events and include audit logs showing when the key was destroyed.

4) Cross-region replication: We can disable replication at the account-level; however, if FintechCo is currently set up in multiple regions we'll need to reconcile existing replicas. New accounts can be provisioned with replication disabled.

I'll draft a short implementation timeline for the deep-dive and include the attestation wording for Legal to review.

- Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FintechCo RTBF / data retention follow-up & next steps

Sarah - thanks for the quick responses and for sending the questionnaire. Per our internal review, high-level proposal attached (MVP-rtbf-proposal.docx) and summary below: 

Proposed mutual action plan (short):
- Day 0: FintechCo submits validated RTBF request via API or portal.
- 0-48 hours: Remove user records from live DB and object store references; confirm via status webhook.
- 0-7 days: Invalidate caches and scrub indexes; provide progress updates.
- For backups: default retention 90 days. If FintechCo requires irrecoverability prior to 90 days, we recommend the Key Shred attestation approach (crypto-shred + signed attestation).

Deliverables for Legal: 
- Attestation template for key-shred events.
- Audit log export showing deletion events and key destruction timestamps.
- Confirmation that replication can be disabled and backups restricted to us-east-1 for your account.

Next actions
1) Please confirm whether FintechCo accepts the key-shred attestation approach or requires a 30-day backup SLA that would require provisioning a separate backup policy.
2) If accepted, please confirm times for a 60-minute technical deep-dive this week (Mateo & Rishi).
3) I will open a HubSpot ticket (HS-4821) and share the mutual action plan + the DocuSign attestation template for Legal to review.

Thanks - looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best regards,
Camila Reyes
